lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Think about a doorknob, a stair step, a keyboard key. Surfaces change as things rub against them. Antoine's master's thesis teaches a computer to show that wear as it happens.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In real time? That sounds demanding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the topic: real-time surface wear in interactive physics simulations, with dynamic friction and textures. It sits where physical simulation, contact and graphics rendering meet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, at ÉTS, in the master's program in Information Technology Engineering, from August 2023 to September 2026. Sheldon Andrews supervised it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the thesis connect to in Antoine's other work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Several threads. A contact model where friction depends on direction and on the pair of materials, which links to his pull requests to IPC Toolkit. TrueMapData, which reads height maps of real worn surfaces. And MistubaVideo, which turns recorded poses and surface fields into frames and video.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the data in, the physics, and the pictures out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nicely put. The work was also presented at GraphQuon in 2024 and 2025.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Plenty of people. Paul Kry, Yinchu Liu, Loïc Nassif, Nicolas Rosset, Quoc-Minh Ton-That, Alexandre Mercier-Aubin and Mélissa Katz all gave advice and help along the way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A technical write-up on wear in texture space is coming soon, and a thesis article already gives the project overview.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The full post has links to every connected project.
